A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SimuHome simulator and benchmark. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across the substantial appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 11 agents on 600 episodes, error analyses, and human validation of LLM judging.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds model evaluations, latency measurements, planning and feedback experiments, fine-tuning results, and scoring-time sensitivity analysis.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 expands the reported agent interface from 13 to 17 tools. Appendix B adds environmental-control-rule retrieval, user questions, workflow cancellation, and workflow-status inspection. The core simulator dynamics and ReAct prompt remain unchanged; Appendix J's simulation-based pre-validation architecture is a future proposal.

E1.justification: The main benchmark retains 600 episodes and the same twelve query types. Appendices F and G extend existing QT2-F and QT4-F tasks to simulated user clarification, corrective dialogue, and explicit post-execution failure feedback. The additional fine-tuning episodes reuse existing query coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains all eleven original models and adds Llama3.2-1B-it, Llama3.2-3B-it, Gemma3-4B-it, Gemini2.5-Pro, and GPT-5.1, substantially extending comparisons to lightweight and reasoning models. Section 5.2.4 also evaluates HiAgent against ReAct, and Table 13 compares fine-tuned and untuned Gemma3-4B-it.

E3.justification: New protocols include episode-completion-time measurement, callback-triggered self-review, simulated-user feedback, and recovery evaluation on initially failed episodes. Appendix H introduces training on 204 gold trajectories from separate generated episodes; Appendix I tests a three-second scoring delay. These are additional experimental settings, not evidence that the retained main-table experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained error taxonomy and tool-feedback analysis, v2 tests framework dependence with HiAgent, autonomous self-review, clarification and correction dialogues, oracle failure notices, memorization through fine-tuning, and sensitivity to delayed state checking. These analyses directly investigate alternative explanations for benchmark failures.

E5.justification: Both versions report three judge calls per case, seeded episode generation, and the same annotation-agreement and judge-validation statistics. v2 adds no repeated-agent-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: The original eleven Table 1 rows and GPT-4.1 error counts are unchanged, but substantial results are added. GPT-5.1 reaches 100% on QT4-1-IF; HiAgent obtains 40%, 52%, and 40% on QT4 feasible tasks. New latency, dialogue, recovery, and fine-tuning results appear. Appendix I reports 62% versus 44% for GPT-4.1 QT2-F when scoring is delayed three seconds, a changed-condition result.

T1.justification: The POMDP formulation in Section 3.3 and additive Aggregator equation remain unchanged, with the latter moving from Appendix A.12 to Appendix P. The new discussions of pre-validation and environmental interactions introduce no formal definitions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The simulator and benchmark contributions remain, but the headline empirical message changes substantially. v1 emphasizes GPT-4.1's leading 54% overall success and general capability deficits. v2's abstract, introduction, and conclusion distinguish lightweight, standard, and reasoning models and introduce performance versus latency as a central deployment trade-off.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning framework versus model limitations, limited self-correction, memorization, and deployment latency. Appendix G explicitly qualifies oracle-assisted recovery as optimistic. Appendix I attributes part of GPT-4.1's QT2-F weakness to transition timing, qualifying the intent-inference interpretation. Appendices J and K discuss future pre-validation and richer environmental interactions.

D1.justification: Appendix N replaces a model-name paragraph with exact API endpoint identifiers. Other additions document tool arguments, user-simulator models, and construction of the 204 training trajectories. These improve implementation specificity, although training hyperparameters remain unreported. The promise to release code and data upon publication is unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Llama 3, GPT-5.1, and HiAgent, including a substantive comparison with HiAgent. The related-work section and positioning against household simulators and smart-home benchmarks are otherwise retained. Updated metadata for existing model references does not constitute new research positioning.

P1.justification: The results narrative is rewritten from query-by-query discussion into model-capability groups. Evaluation methods move into benchmark design, and analysis becomes part of experiments. The appendix is extensively reorganized into A–Q, grouping error analyses and prompts, while the abstract and conclusion are rewritten around the new empirical narrative.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains model-category divisions; v2 adds the HiAgent figure and latency, self-review, oracle-recovery, and fine-tuning tables. Appendix tables and prompt listings undergo extensive font, spacing, and multipage-layout changes. The original QT3 error-distribution figure is retained as Figure 7 with changed placement and size.

improvement.justification: v1's failure interpretations relied largely on one framework and descriptive error analysis. v2 directly tests framework choice, feedback availability, training, and scoring time, substantially improving the evidence available to assess benchmark validity. Reasoning-model and latency comparisons also strengthen deployment relevance. Sparse experimental settings and broad causal and memorization conclusions remain weaknesses, but the new controls and disclosed scoring-time confound provide substantial diagnostic gains.
